routed.text: ADR-001 is amended, not superseded (DEC-018, DEC-019): booking-api@v1 takes auth-api@v1's bearer token from the in-memory store; sessions are never in PostgreSQL; there is no logout endpoint. Its Consequences make a missing, unknown or expired token one case at every endpoint that takes the token, 401 UNAUTHORIZED, so booking-api@v1's endpoints answer it with the same envelope profile-api gives. ADR-001's affects already names booking-api@v1: its front matter needs governed_by: [ADR-001, ADR-002], or gate C3's forward-reference warning becomes an error once the file exists.

ADR-001 keeps in-memory sessions and client-side sign-out (DEC-018, DEC-019), so its update asks nothing of auth-api@v1's guarantees on a restart or sign-out beyond what they already rest on. If the touch restates the token guarantee ('accepted ... until expiresAt'), a restart ending every token early is existing behavior (ADR-001 Consequences, first bullet), a clarification rather than a new rule. auth-api@v1's front matter already carries governed_by: [ADR-001] (Q-001).

ADR-001's affects now names simple-login (execution plan C-2, DEC-022), so the root header must keep Governed by: [ADR-001] when the touch restates it, or gate C3 errors. The Decisions bullet on ADR-001 (in-memory sessions, 30 minutes, sign-out on the client) stays true under the amendment.

ADR-001 keeps sessions in memory (DEC-018), so simple-login.integration.2's restart stays a valid expired-token stand-in for AC-2.3 and the intake record's 'revisited if ADR-001's update makes sessions survive a restart' does not fire. The PRD v2 Success test that a restart keeps every booking must sign in again after the restart, since the same restart signs every user out (ADR-001 Consequences).

notes: Outcome: ADR-001 amended, not superseded. Sessions stay in the in-memory store, so a restart still signs every user out (DEC-018); sign-out stays client-side with no logout endpoint (DEC-019). Decision text unchanged; Consequences gain two bullets and two clauses (DEC-020); Context kept as history with a one-paragraph pointer to Amendments (DEC-021).

Superseding was weighed and set aside partly because the next ADR number is ADR-002, which H2 already names for the time model; had it been chosen, one of the two would have needed renumbering in the intake record.

would_upstream: DEC-018 and DEC-019 carry it. RFC-001 §3 still gives 'no database' as the reason a restart may sign everybody out and says to revisit sign-out if the API grows; both choices stand with new reasons, which RFC-001's authors should record. This is the same upstream item as DEC-013.

DEC-015 expected H1 to rewrite ADR-001's 'The PRD needs' sentence. DEC-021 keeps the Context as written (the step's rule against rewriting history) and adds a pointer; the cites-superseded experiment found no baseline-path citation in ADR-001, so no citation touch is owed.
